requirements.section: 7. Durable history and uniform creative intelligence
requirements.requirement: The CSV creative tables reconstruct the normalized creative catalog, source assets, exact renditions, components, palettes, deployments, and performance joins without a lossy wide row. Imported/provider media is either transient or retained only in an explicitly configured local vault, and sensitive-data scans run before persistence or export.
requirements.remaining: Redacted record-node reconstruction, complete serving-manifest digest projection, private bounded asset reads and no-overwrite fsynced publication have local fixture evidence. Full creative child-table coverage, provider media policy, retention/availability observations and cross-platform vault implementation remain incomplete.

requirements.requirement: Reproducible signed binaries run on the documented supported macOS, Windows, and Linux versions; a pinned OCI image is also reproducible.
requirements.remaining: Two actual unsigned native development builds match for one fixed arm64 macOS toolchain and synthetic build configuration. Signed supported-platform binaries, pinned OCI, release manifests and exact release reproducibility evidence remain required. Paired Python/native development artifacts have offline source/configuration binding coverage only; release signing, installation and capability authority remain unproven. The explicit Meta build profile and canonical pair comparator have fake-only review coverage; two exact unsigned Meta-profile builds match all nine files under the declared local toolchain; release evidence remains open.

requirements.requirement: Release checksums, SBOM, dependency and license scans, and provenance attestations ship with each maintained build.
requirements.remaining: Reusable exact-commit development validation produces reproducible wheel/source hashes and a runtime-lock-only CycloneDX graph. Final per-artifact release SBOM, maintained-platform dependency/license scans, signed provenance/checksums and actual release publication remain required.

requirements.requirement: Fresh-machine install, initialization, optional signed update check, update- check opt-out, upgrade, and uninstall work without engineering help.
requirements.remaining: Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: Every build discloses its release status separately from provider support and credential permissions: which commands are available, which remote-mutation commands are `UNRELEASED`, and each provider's release label. There are no editions or tiers. A build that has not released writes refuses every remote mutation at one release-policy gate, before credential-store access, ledger `APPLY_STARTED`, or network egress, even with broader provider credentials. Audit and report checks cannot mutate provider state or initiate browser measurement traffic, and findings, history, and safe exports stay useful in every build. See [`release-0.1.0.md`](release-0.1.0.md).
requirements.remaining: Rewritten in O4.2c for the free open-source model; it replaces DOD-8-ec381fed9e and carries that requirement's annotations. The configured edition was removed by O3.2 under ADR 0013. Provider mutation is refused by the 0.1.0 release-policy gate (src/adhelm/release_policy.py) before keys, native approval or provider calls: in the declared execution and recovery commands, at the entry of each retained execution workflow, and at SafetyKernel.execute and record_attempt_recovery. Read, report, audit and planning commands without remote effect remain available, and discovery, doctor and provider-naming outputs carry each provider's release label (src/adhelm/release_labels.py). The gate has fake-only coverage in tests/test_release_policy.py and tests/test_release_labels.py and is described in docs/implementation/release-policy-gate.md and docs/implementation/provider-release-labels.md. Live/platform evidence for any later release of writes remains required.

requirements.requirement: AdHelm is free software under Apache-2.0 ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-open-source-release.md)). There is no paid tier, license key, trial, vendor-registered provider application, token relay, or paid support, and no runtime license service, heartbeat, or meter on commands, executions, accounts, spend, rows, or API calls. A build stays runnable indefinitely. Users register their own provider applications from a documented per-provider setup guide and bring their own credentials. Upstream incompatibility is reported honestly.
requirements.remaining: Rewritten in O4.2c; it replaces DOD-8-d40410da08. ADR 0013 records the free Apache-2.0 decision and docs/release-0.1.0.md the bring-your-own-app setup gate, but no source file, license text or package metadata is evidenced yet (O4.3 adds LICENSE, NOTICE and metadata; O4.2a and O4.2b add the per-provider setup guides) and the absence of a runtime license service or meter has no dedicated test. Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: Upgrades preserve verified history and profile continuity. Shared schema changes cannot silently strand retained builds or interrupted work; supported migration/export and guarded recovery paths are documented/tested.
requirements.remaining: Rewritten in O4.2c to drop the word edition; it replaces DOD-8-59bc19938d. Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: Upstream provider quotas, approvals, access tiers, breaking changes, and certification requirements are disclosed as external constraints.
requirements.remaining: Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: Versioned agent instructions, schemas, capabilities, examples, noninteractive structured results, and actionable diagnostics implement the primary agent interface in [`lifecycle-contract.md`](lifecycle-contract.md#agent-facing-interface-and-human-artifacts). A deterministic caller exercises it without an external model in default CI.
requirements.remaining: Installed discovery/schema/guidance now includes closed local image/text registration and checkpoint-backed redacted creative review. The deterministic installed-wheel validator exercises analyze/register/retry/catalog/show without external models or credentials. Complete lifecycle commands, all output/status cases, cross-platform packaging and external-host validation remain required.

requirements.requirement: Agent-mode checks cover output bounds/pagination, no silent truncation, stable outcome/exit semantics, missing auth/approval without terminal hangs, pending-operation status checks, interrupted execution, and reconciliation of ambiguity without mutation replay.
requirements.remaining: Installed typed inputs reject unsafe files and scalar aliases before effects. Explicit OpenAI pause/GA4 CREATE command tests cover static discovery, default binding refusal before keys/native/provider calls, complete preflighted redacted output and fixed verified/partial/ambiguous/no-effect exits. Unconfigured native executables refuse within bounded time. Complete pending-operation and interruption flows, platform behavior, signed installation, real host interaction and live provider evidence remain required.

requirements.requirement: Primary usability validation includes marketers without CLI experience directing a customer-selected agent through report, diagnosis, plan, preferred review, direct or delegated authorization, execution, and verification. They need not type commands, construct JSON, or copy digests. Record host/version, time, founder/support intervention, failures, and confusion through consented local evidence. Named Claude Code/Codex compatibility claims require successful validation in that host; fixture-only checks do not prove the experience.
requirements.remaining: Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: User-configurable artifact modes, purposes, workflow-stage rules, formats, local destinations, detail bounds, reuse, and overwrite policy pass validation. Tests cover compact/on-request defaults, `OFF`, task overrides without changing saved defaults, rule matching, unchanged-input reuse, unsupported formats, missing destinations, and no implicit scheduling or remote upload.
requirements.remaining: Local JSON/CSV/HTML report/audit, measurement-comparison and retained OpenAI pause/GA4 CREATE/Meta campaign PAUSE plan artifacts have deterministic policy, reuse, closed-source and partial-output fixtures. GA4 and Meta saved plan-review rules and explicit historical rendering preserve no-authority facts. Remaining workflow stages, required presentation formats, cross-platform execution and named-host usability remain incomplete.

requirements.requirement: Both compact inline review with optional artifacts disabled and requested/rule- selected artifact workflows are usable. Optional files can explain findings, compare options, review integration plans, and report outcomes. Canonical source references persist independently of presentation; required review facts, plans, approvals, and durable history cannot be disabled by token or artifact preferences. No exact external-host token/billing cap is claimed.
requirements.remaining: Installed compact retained-plan receipts and full inline review coexist with explicit/saved-rule static plan artifacts. Fixtures preserve source/checkpoint references and retained plans/completed files on partial output failures; current validity and authority remain separate. Full integration/execution/verification presentation and actual agent-led usability remain required.

requirements.requirement: The versioned optimization skill package follows [`agent-skills.md`](agent-skills.md). Both skill folders and their referenced resources are bundled with release digests and tested CLI/schema compatibility. Offline scenarios validate evidence discipline, conversion semantics, output preferences, progressive loading, and absent/unsupported CLI behavior. Named- host usability evidence separately proves the skills work with that host; default skill checks require no external model, account, or provider calls.
requirements.remaining: Both authored skills and named references ship in development wheels and are locally discoverable with bounded progressive CLI output. Offline deterministic scenario coverage exists in tests/test_skill_scenarios.py (stale vocabulary, named commands, options and schemas, release-scope handling, the refused apply-a-recommendation scenario and verification by reading again). Exact release digests, installed named-agent compatibility and marketer usability remain required.

requirements.requirement: Negative cases include invented commands, stale instructions, unsafe fixes, injected provider instructions, misleading AI-written spend summaries, edited spreadsheets, stale HTML reviews, and malicious action links. None can bypass canonical plan validation, direct/delegated authorization, drift rejection, or the existing data/export boundary. Artifact edits proposing operational changes require recompilation and new approval; presentation edits do not change the canonical plan or approval. Opening a file/link never performs a remote mutation.
requirements.remaining: Independent artifact regressions cover forged nested authority, invalid numeric control aliases, changed handoff sources, unsafe destinations and static historical rendering. These local renderer checks do not exercise every malicious host/document interaction or installed direct/delegated execution; complete negative-case and live/host evidence remain required.

requirements.requirement: Agent-visible outputs and artifacts use the existing redacted sharing policy. The selected agent's possible model egress is disclosed; raw payloads, credentials, and prohibited fields do not appear in its output or hidden artifact content. The CLI never automatically invokes an assistant. The deterministic core, secondary direct path, and default tests work without an AI account; that independence does not replace agent-led usability validation.
requirements.remaining: Selected agent report/plan/reference and JSON/CSV/HTML artifact paths use keyed closed sharing projections, preserve no-authority facts, and have independent offline secret-leak regressions. Google OAuth lifecycle and GA4 source bindings use synthetic fixtures only. Complete presentation/provider coverage, real credential lifecycle, cross-platform execution and no-AI-account/agent-host usability remain required.

requirements.requirement: Maintenance runs in the open under documented boundaries: [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md) states how changes are proposed and reviewed, and [`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) states how vulnerabilities are reported. No paid support, optional service delivery, or sale of the tool or brand is a requirement for product completion.
requirements.remaining: Rewritten in O4.2c for the open-source model; it replaces DOD-8-004154f14b. The contribution, vulnerability-reporting and conduct policies exist and are tested for their required content. GitHub private vulnerability reporting, branch protection and the DCO check are owner and O4.3 actions that are not yet in effect. Implementation and required evidence pending.

The resulting ledger passes `history verify` throughout the soak.

A cross-platform comparison of one shared creative family proves exact-version joins and preserves provider-specific delivery caveats.

requirements.requirement: One integrated acceptance starts from a single `StrategyBrief` targeting all six live test profiles, produces a unified inventory/report and evidence- backed recommendation, compiles all six subplans before any write, and binds one composite approval to every displayed subplan digest. A controlled test- harness transport fault then produces a verified no-effect failure for one provider after at least one earlier paused/draft subplan succeeds; the run stops under its declared policy, consumes started authorizations, reconciles every provider, emits complete partial-outcome evidence, creates a new plan for any remaining work, and safely archives/restores all test entities. A second clean run proves the happy path. No fault is injected into a provider after its mutation request begins.
requirements.remaining: Implementation and required evidence pending.

requirements.requirement: Failure drills cover expired auth, insufficient scope, rate limits, pagination interruption, malformed/partial responses, stale plans, remote drift, partial success, ambiguous timeouts, revoked access, network loss, provider review, and asynchronous completion.
requirements.remaining: Local fixtures cover selected transport and malformed-response failures; required provider live drills remain absent.

requirements.requirement: Thirty consecutive calendar days run the scheduled `doctor`, `report`, `audit`, GA4 health, and configured GTM health checks against validation profiles. A day counts only when every scheduled job runs and no product defect loses data or reports a false healthy state. Documented upstream downtime may count only when correctly detected/classified and recovered within provider policy.
